recentItems.title: Trump: "I Convinced" Nvidia's Board To Bring Huang Back. What You Need To Know
recentItems.description:
James Longman reports on the unexpected comeback of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Plus, the nearly five tons of explosives detonated in Iowa, with the explosion heard for miles. And history on the dance floor, as 'Dancing with the Stars' saw a first-of-its-kind winner. Those headlines and more stories you need to know.

00:27: NVIDIA FALLOUT: Just 11 days after stepping down, Jensen Huang is back as CEO. Trump says a pardon for Huang is "always an option." Huang has apologized to employees as he prepares to face questions from three congressional committees about his alleged affair.
01:34: TRUMP IN AZ NEXT WEEK: The president is expected to attend a groundbreaking ceremony for an expansion of TSMC's chip manufacturing operations.
01:53: IA DETONATION SAGA: The head of the EPA says no lead has been detected in the air so far and that the agency will continue testing the air, water, and soil for weeks.
02:17: ANOTHER MEASLES DEATH: The U.S. has now reported 14 measles-related deaths this year.
03:16: 'AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY' TRAILER: The film's trailer has become Disney's most-watched ever.
04:04: A.I. AGENTS AND SHOPPING: Meta has teamed up with Walmart this Black Friday, allowing shoppers to link a credit card so an A.I. agent can make purchases on their behalf.
04:43: MALL OF AMERICA/SHOPPING FORECAST: The Mall of America is attempting a Guinness World Record this Black Friday, while Adobe predicts the biggest shopping day of the season will bring in $13 billion.
05:21: HOTTEST GIFTS OF THE SEASON: Google released its Holiday 100 list, revealing top search trends that include the FAO Schwarz Piano Mat, perfume gift sets, and Polaroid cameras.
06:03: 'DANCING WITH THE STARS' WINNER: Ezra Frech has made history on the show, becoming the first amputee to win the competition.
